title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth The Indication Of Order In The Cosmos To Unity

questions.question: What main idea is taught in this passage about the One who runs the universe?
questions.answer: He is one and alone, and He takes care of everything in the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the universe itself that helps show this truth?
questions.answer: It says the universe has strong order, balance, and regular patterns.

questions.question: How do the parts of the universe work with the whole?
questions.answer: They fit into one big system and work together in an organized way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Divine Names and actions at work in the world?
questions.answer: They reach across everything or almost everything, not just one small part.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that many things are alike in nature and found in many places?
questions.answer: To show that one plan and one command are at work everywhere.

questions.question: What picture is used for the world to help us understand this idea?
questions.answer: The world is described like a grand city and a beautifully made palace.

questions.question: According to the passage, does the One who made the cosmos need helpers or partners?
questions.answer: No. He has no helper, partner, equal, or rival.

questions.question: What does the passage say order shows by itself?
questions.answer: Order itself points to one organizer.

questions.question: Why is sharing rule between many gods rejected in this passage?
questions.answer: Because partners would bring conflict and disorder, not perfect order.

questions.question: If everything is arranged with care in one system, what can we infer about its Maker?
questions.answer: We can infer that the Maker is unique, fully in control, and not many.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that this truth is very clear and certain?
questions.answer: It says the truth is necessary and obvious.

questions.question: What is one good summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The perfect order and unity in creation show that Allah alone is the Maker and Ruler of all.

questions.question: What does the title “The Fifth Truth” introduce?
questions.answer: It introduces a new proof about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Who is said to notice this truth in the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler notices it at the second stage.

questions.question: What is seen throughout the universe according to this section?
questions.answer: A very complete order and regular system is seen everywhere.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the things used in running this huge world?
questions.answer: They are similar in kind and work for clear purposes in the same overall plan.

questions.question: How are the Divine Names and actions described in relation to all things?
questions.answer: They are said to surround and include all things or most things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about elements and species on the earth?
questions.answer: They are spread all over the earth even though the same kinds appear in many places.

questions.question: Why is the spread of the same kinds across the earth important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows one Maker is managing everything with one rule.

questions.question: What titles are given to the One who made and manages the universe?
questions.answer: He is described as Maker, Manager, King, Nurturer, Master, and Builder.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah compared with all others?
questions.answer: It teaches that He is one, unique, and alone, with no equal.

questions.question: What weaknesses does the passage deny about Him?
questions.answer: It denies that He has any weakness or any lack.

questions.question: What is the connection between order and unity in this passage?
questions.answer: Order points to unity because one well-arranged system needs one arranger.

questions.question: What is the final lesson a student should learn from this passage?
questions.answer: The harmony of the universe teaches that only one Lord is in charge of all creation.

questions.question: What quality of the cosmos is mentioned first in this passage?
questions.answer: Its complete order and regularity.

questions.question: Besides the whole cosmos, what other levels are included in this order?
questions.answer: Its main supports, smaller parts, and all the beings inside it.

questions.question: How are the substances and living things in the universe described?
questions.answer: They are described as alike in many ways and serving meaningful purposes.

questions.question: What does it mean that these things are connected to one general scheme?
questions.answer: It means they belong to one overall plan.

questions.question: How are the Divine Names and deeds working in the world described?
questions.answer: They work through everything widely and in a way that covers all or most things.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the same names and deeds appear in every place?
questions.answer: It suggests one Lord is acting everywhere.

questions.question: What is special about the elements and species mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They are found across the whole earth and still remain part of one system.

questions.question: If the same type of element or species is found in many places, what does that support?
questions.answer: It supports the idea of one Creator and one way of managing creation.

questions.question: What four words best describe the One who controls the cosmos in this section?
questions.answer: One, unique, sole, and unmatched.

questions.question: Which relationships are denied for Him in the passage?
questions.answer: It denies that He has a partner, assistant, equal, or opposite.

questions.question: Why would multiple rulers not fit the universe described here?
questions.answer: Because many rulers would lead to disagreements, but the universe shows harmony and order.

questions.question: What conclusion does the whole passage lead the reader to?
questions.answer: The organized universe clearly proves Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does this passage use as evidence to teach about Allah?
questions.answer: It uses the order, sameness, and wide reach of creation.

questions.question: What does “regularity” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means things happen in a steady, arranged, and consistent way.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk about things being nested within each other and still being alike?
questions.answer: To show that one rule covers different layers of creation at the same time.

questions.question: What do the Divine Names and deeds do in this passage?
questions.answer: They operate broadly through the world and reach into many things.

questions.question: How is the earth described when speaking about elements and species?
questions.answer: It is described as being covered by them.

questions.question: What does the passage say these signs “demand” or strongly require us to accept?
questions.answer: That the One who made and manages everything is one and without partner.

questions.question: What examples of roles are given for this One Lord?
questions.answer: He is spoken of as the one who makes, manages, rules, raises, and builds.

questions.question: What does the passage say He does not have besides partners?
questions.answer: He does not have an equal, a helper, an opposite, weakness, or any shortcoming.

questions.question: Why is order called a sign of unity?
questions.answer: Because a well-ordered system shows one guiding will behind it.

questions.question: What bad results are linked with claiming partners for Allah?
questions.answer: Disagreement and disorder.

questions.question: Is the proof in this passage based on confusion or clarity? Explain.
questions.answer: It is based on clarity, because the passage says the signs are obvious and certain.

questions.question: How could a Muslim student put the message of this passage into one sentence?
questions.answer: The beautiful order of the world shows that Allah alone is the Lord of everything.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be seen in all of the universe and its parts?
questions.answer: A perfect system of order and arrangement.

questions.question: How are the beings in the universe linked to one another?
questions.answer: They are connected as parts of one shared plan.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the names and actions of Allah in the world?
questions.answer: They are active in a broad way and include everything or nearly everything.

questions.question: Why is it important that the same kinds of things are found in many places on earth?
questions.answer: Because that points to one source and one controller.

questions.question: What images are used for the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: It is compared to a kingdom, a city, and a palace.

questions.question: What do those images help us understand?
questions.answer: They help us understand that the universe is run in an organized and planned way.

questions.question: According to the passage, who is the ruler and caretaker of this kingdom?
questions.answer: The one and only Allah.

questions.question: What does “sole” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means He is alone in His rule and has no sharer.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about needing assistants?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah does not need assistants or ministers.

questions.question: How does the passage connect unity with peace in the system of the world?
questions.answer: One ruler brings harmony, while partners would bring conflict.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is used in this section?
questions.answer: It reasons from the order in creation to the oneness of the Creator.

questions.question: What is the best overall conclusion from the passage?
questions.answer: The united system of the world proves there is only one true Lord over all.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah is one and has no partner.

questions.question: What signs in creation are used to explain this truth?
questions.answer: The signs are order, regular patterns, shared design, and wide spread of the same kinds of things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the universe as a whole and its smaller parts?
questions.answer: Both the whole universe and its smaller parts show the same organized care.

questions.question: How do the Divine Names and deeds help prove the main message?
questions.answer: Their work appears broadly and in the same way across creation, showing one source.

questions.question: What is the point of saying the same elements and species are present across the earth?
questions.answer: It shows that one power controls them all everywhere.

questions.question: What names for Allah’s relationship to creation are mentioned here?
questions.answer: He is described as the Maker, Manager, King, Nurturer, Master, and Builder.

questions.question: What does the passage clearly deny about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: It denies any partner, helper, equal, rival, weakness, or defect.

questions.question: Why does the passage say order cannot leave room for partners?
questions.answer: Because true order needs one organizer, not many competing rulers.

questions.question: What would likely happen if there were many gods in charge, based on this passage?
questions.answer: There would be dispute and confusion instead of harmony.

questions.question: Is the argument in this passage only a guess, or is it presented as certain?
questions.answer: It is presented as certain and clear.

questions.question: How does this passage help strengthen iman for a young Muslim reader?
questions.answer: It teaches that when we look at the world’s order, we can recognize Allah’s oneness more clearly.

questions.question: What is a strong summary statement for this whole section?
questions.answer: Since the universe runs with one perfect system, its Lord must be one, unique, and unmatched.
